claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a native, heterogeneous oxide scale.
The continuity of Q235 steel's native oxide scale governs its corrosion resistance.
The phase composition of Q235 steel's native oxide scale governs its corrosion resistance.
A uniform and stable oxide layer protects Q235 steel against salt-induced corrosion at room temperature.
A uniform and stable oxide layer protects Q235 steel against salt-induced corrosion at 700–900 °C.
Disruption or transformation of the oxide layer accelerates Q235 degradation during aggressive high-temperature salt exposure.
Annealing temperature and duration can modify the thickness, uniformity, and composition of Q235 steel's native oxide layer.
The study will compare annealed Q235 specimens with untreated, as-received controls.
The comparison will be conducted in 0.5–1 M NaCl at room temperature and in an aggressive salt at 700–900 °C.
An intact, uniform oxide scale limits ion transport.
An intact, uniform oxide scale limits oxidation reactions.
High-temperature oxide phase changes or spallation cause barrier failure and accelerate corrosion.
Optimized annealing can reinforce the protective oxide scale, whereas excessive annealing can disturb it.
Q235 samples with an optimally reinforced oxide will exhibit lower mass change than untreated controls.
Q235 samples with an optimally reinforced oxide will exhibit fewer corrosion pits than untreated controls.
Q235 samples with an optimally reinforced oxide will exhibit better electrochemical impedance responses than untreated controls.
Q235 samples with compromised oxide layers will corrode faster than the untreated baseline.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to steels with different oxide-forming tendencies or to conditions that do not induce significant oxide transformations.
The annealing temperatures and durations needed to produce an optimal Q235 oxide scale are not defined.
Absence of statistically significant corrosion improvement or absence of a correlation between oxide integrity and corrosion performance would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis allows annealing to improve or impair protection and states that the optimal annealing conditions are unknown, yet lack of improvement from the selected annealing treatment is declared sufficient to falsify the mechanism. A null result could instead mean that the treatment failed to produce the proposed reinforced oxide.
